name: ros_graph_debugger
description: Runtime DevTools for ROS 2 — live graph, bottleneck detection, callback tracing, AI briefings, and a fleet view.

paragraphs: Data flows along the graph; then the detector stalls — its node turns red, readiness goes ERROR, and its pipeline path lights up the rate and callback bottleneck. Try it live →

Runtime DevTools for ROS 2. A live, AI-friendly view of your running ROS 2 system: the graph, topic rate / bandwidth / message size, QoS, TF freshness, diagnostics — and an issue panel that tells you where to look next.

Not a replacement for rqtgraph. It overlays runtime metrics and bottleneck detection on the graph, and exposes everything as a web view, JSON, Markdown, and an MCP server so AI assistants can debug your robot with you.
features: Live ROS graph with auto layout (pub → topic → sub) and animated data

flow — dashes march along each edge at a speed set by the topic's rate, and bottleneck nodes pulse a red halo (toggle with ✨ Flow). Plus a Network view — a sortable/filterable table of every topic (rate, bandwidth, p95…
Topic metrics: rate, bandwidth, avg / p95 message size (opt-in probing).
QoS mismatch detection — the classic "connected but no data flows" trap,

across every request/offer policy DDS checks: reliability, durability, deadline, liveliness kind and lease duration. The issue names the failing pair and policy (e.g. /lidar → /fusion: deadline: publisher offers 200 ms,…
